evidence: Reviewed staged diff (3 tracked files): picap auto-accept service-type filter (OMS/Mostrador/Todos) added to OrderStateManager, shouldAutoAccept gate, and segmented selector in the Picap tab

Traced the only Picap auto-accept entry point (MyAccessibilityService.kt:320 isPicapAutoAcceptEnabled && shouldAutoAccept) and confirmed the WhatsApp auto-accept path (NotificationInterceptorService / whatsapp* settings) is untouched

findings.claim: Classification relies solely on servicio containing the substring 'Mostrador'; empty or reworded servicio strings classify as OMS, so a MOSTRADOR filter would silently auto-accept nothing if Picap renames the field content. Mirrors the existing card-title fallback, but there is no log when zero orders match a filter.
proof_refs: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderCard.kt:77 card title uses the same contains("Mostrador") fallback to OMS

findings.claim: picapAutoAcceptFilter persists an unvalidated string from SharedPreferences; a corrupted or legacy value (e.g. lowercase 'oms') silently disables the filter branch and behaves as TODOS. Acceptable default-on-failure behavior, but an enum or whitelist normalization on load would make it explicit.
proof_refs: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderStateManager.kt:65 loadAll reads the pref without validating against OMS/MOSTRADOR/TODOS

findings.claim: The selector only renders while isPicapAutoAcceptEnabled is true, so the configured filter is invisible when auto-accept is off; a user cannot verify the pending filter without toggling the switch. Intentional to mirror the km-slider pattern, noted for UX awareness.
proof_refs: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MainActivity.kt:513 selector rendered only while isPicapAutoAcceptEnabled is true
